newsitem.title: UK: House of Fraser sets one year deadline.
newsitem.headline: House of Fraser sets one year deadline.

text.p: British department store group House of Fraser executives said on Thursday they expected to see improvements from restructuring in a year and chairman Brian McGowan staked his job on it.
"It will be precisely in one year's time that we will know (whether changes have brought improvements). That may well be the time for the swords to come out," he told a news conference on Thursday.
House of Fraser earlier reported year pretax profits of 14.8 million stg before exceptionals for restructuring of 53.2 million stg, compared with a profit of 14.3 million stg previously.
The group has implemented refurbishments and wide ranging changes including the planned launch of a new own-label range in an effort to revive its flagging fortunes.
Chief executive John Coleman said the group would be looking for a quick success from the changes.
"There is an awful lot to go for," McGowan said, pointing out that every one percentage point improvement in gross profit margins meant an extra six million stg of profit.
House of Fraser was floated by the Fayed brothers, owners of London's landmark Harrods store in 1994.
It has since floundered against competition and McGowan conceded that the last three years "hasn't been a happy story for shareholders and I can assure you it hasn't been a happy story for me."
Coleman said the chain aimed to cut the amount of time its stores discounted in sales from 23 weeks last year to 18 weeks this year.
He added that the changes which the group had made should mean it could "look forward to a period of sustained sales and earnings growth."
